sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Field scabious is a herbaceous perennial native to Europe and temperate Asia, common in fairly dry meadows and along roadsides. Its upright stems reach about 15–60 cm.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The leaves are opposite, often lobed near the base and narrower higher on the stem. The lilac-blue flower heads are about 2–4 cm across. Each flower produces a dry achene about 5–6 mm long.

sections.title: Pollinators and use
sections.text: The flowers provide nectar for insects, including butterflies. No well-supported food use or particular toxicity was found for this species.
